facts.statement: Nemegtosaurus was a sauropod dinosaur that lived in what is now Mongolia during the Late Cretaceous Period.
facts.quote: Nemegtosaurus (meaning "reptile from the Nemegt") was a sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Period of what is now Mongolia.

facts.statement: Nemegtosaurus was estimated to measure between 12 and 13 meters long and weigh 20 tonnes.
facts.quote: Measuring an estimated 12 - 13 m long and weighing 20 t

facts.statement: The genus was named after the Nemegt Basin in the Gobi Desert, where only a single skull was found.
facts.quote: it was named after the Nemegt Basin in the Gobi Desert, where the remains — a single skull — were found.

facts.statement: The skull of Nemegtosaurus was long and low, resembling diplodocoids, and possessed pencil-shaped teeth.
facts.quote: The skull resembles diplodocoids in being long and low, with pencil-shaped teeth.

facts.statement: Recent studies have classified Nemegtosaurus as a titanosaur closely related to Saltasaurus, Alamosaurus, and Rapetosaurus.
facts.quote: However, recent work has shown that Nemegtosaurus is in fact a titanosaur, closely related to animals such as Saltasaurus, Alamosaurus, and Rapetosaurus.

facts.statement: A second species, N. pachi, was described by Dong in 1977 based on teeth from the Subashi Formation, but it is considered a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: A second species, N. pachi, was described by Dong in 1977 on the basis of the teeth IVPP V.4879, recovered from the Subashi Formation, but this non-diagnostic species is considered a nomen dubium and cannot be referred to Nemegtosauridae.

facts.statement: In 2019, Averianov and Lopatin determined that Nemegtosaurus and Opisthocoelicaudia were not synonymous because shared characters were difficult to determine or based on misidentified specimens.
facts.quote: In 2019, Alexander O. Averianov and Alexey V. Lopatin in a paper describing new specimens of Nemegtosaurus reanalyzed the argument for synonymy and determined that the taxa were not synonymous because shared characters between the species were either difficult to determine or based on comparisons with a specimen which actually belonged to Nemegtosaurus.

facts.statement: Nemegtosaurus lived in the Maastrichtian (66-72 million years ago) Nemegt Formation, making it one of the last sauropods on Earth.
facts.quote: Nemegtosaurus is found in the Maastrichtian aged (66-72 Ma) Nemegt Formation, which makes it one of the last sauropods on earth.

facts.statement: Nemegtosaurus lived on a lush river delta in the Gobi Desert alongside animals such as Gallimimus, Mononykus, Adasaurus, Therizinosaurus, and Tarbosaurus.
facts.quote: There, on a lush river delta flowing through the ancient sands of the Gobi Desert, Nemegtosaurus would have coexisted with animals like the ornithomimid Gallimimus, the alvarezsaurid Mononykus, the velociraptorine Adasaurus, and the giant, saber-clawed therizinosaur Therizinosaurus. It also lived alongside the tyrannosaur Tarbosaurus.

facts.statement: Like other titanosaurs, Nemegtosaurus had slender, pencil-like teeth ground to a sharp, chisel-like tip.
facts.quote: Like other titanosaurs, the teeth are slender pencil-like structures that are ground down at a sharp angle to produce a chisel-like tip.

facts.statement: It is unclear whether Nemegtosaurus browsed high in trees or grazed on low plants, as related titanosaurs exhibit both feeding strategies.
facts.quote: Neither is it clear whether Nemegtosaurus browsed high in the trees or grazed on low-growing plants; related titanosaurs include both long-necked browsing forms like Rapetosaurus and short-necked forms like Bonitasaura.

facts.statement: An adult Nemegtosaurus, with a possible length of 12 meters, may have been able to defend itself against Tarbosaurus, while juveniles would have been vulnerable.
facts.quote: With its possible body length of 12 m, an adult Nemegtosaurus may have been able to defend against Tarbosaurus, but juveniles would have been vulnerable.

facts.statement: Nemegtosaurus is classified within the family Saltasauridae.
Nemegtosaurus belongs to the subfamily Nemegtosaurinae.
Nemegtosaurus lived at the end of the Cretaceous Period, approximately 83 to 65 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 83 y 65 millones de años, en el Campaniense y el Maastrichtiense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: Nemegtosaurus acquired its current status as a titanosaur in the subfamily Nemegtosaurinae within Saltasauridae after 2004.
facts.quote: No fue hasta 2004 cuando el cráneo de Bonitasaura y Rapetosaurus fueran asignados firmemente a Titanosauria, que Nemegtosaurus adquiriera su actual estatus, en él se erige la subfamilia Nemegtosaurinae dentro se Saltasauridae para contenerlos.

facts.statement: It has been proposed that the skull actually belongs to Opisthocoelicaudia, although the postcranial skeleton of that genus clearly belongs to a different family.
facts.quote: Se ha propuesto que el cráneo pertenece ralmente a Opisthocoelicaudia, aunque el esqueleto postcraneal de este pertenece a otra familia claramente.

facts.statement: The rediscovery of the Nemegtosaurus type locality and discovery of comparable postcranial remains have reopened the debate that Opisthocoelicaudia might be a junior synonym of Nemegtosaurus.
facts.quote: El redescubrimiento de la localidad tipo de Nemegtosaurus en el centro de Sayr y descubrimiento de restos postcraneales comparables al holotipo de Opisthocoelicauda ha reabierto el debate la posibilidad de que Opisthocoelicauda sea un sinónimo más moderno.

facts.statement: The time range for Nemegtosaurus is estimated from the Coniacian to the Maastrichtian (89.8 to 66 million years ago).
facts.quote: Time range: Coniacian to Maastrichtian (89.8 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The type species Nemegtosaurus mongoliensis was first described by Nowinski in 1971 based on the specimen ZPAL MgD-I/9.
rejected.quote: The type species, Nemegtosaurus mongoliensis, was first described by Nowinski in 1971 on the basis of ZPAL MgD-I/9.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'The type species Nemegtosaurus mongoliensis was first described'

rejected.statement: Comparisons of scleral rings suggest Nemegtosaurus may have been cathemeral, active throughout the day at short intervals.
rejected.quote: Comparisons between the scleral rings of Nemegtosaurus and modern birds and reptiles suggest that it may have been cathemeral, active throughout the day at short intervals.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'may have been cathemeral active throughout the day'
